title: File system (fs)
lede: Node's fs, ported from lib/fs.js to TypeScript: the synchronous functions, their callback and promise forms, FileHandle, the file streams and fs.watch. Each operation is one native request — on the calling thread for a *Sync function, on the thread pool with the callback on the event loop otherwise — as libuv's are.

entries.name: fs.readFileSync(path[, options])
entries.signature: readFileSync(path: PathOrFileDescriptor, options?: BufferEncoding | { encoding?, flag? }): string | Buffer
entries.description: Reads the whole file: a Buffer of its exact bytes with no encoding, a string decoded in any Buffer encoding with one. A file descriptor reads to its end (readFileSync(0, 'utf8') is stdin). Errors are Node's system errors, with code, errno, syscall and path. Node's lib/fs.js, ported to TypeScript over one native request per operation.

entries.name: fs.writeFileSync / fs.appendFileSync
entries.signature: writeFileSync(file: PathOrFileDescriptor, data: string | ArrayBufferView, options?: WriteFileOptions): void
entries.description: Writes (or appends) a string in any encoding or any ArrayBufferView to a path or descriptor, with Node's { encoding, mode, flag, flush } options.

entries.name: fs.existsSync / fs.accessSync
entries.signature: existsSync(path: PathLike): boolean; accessSync(path: PathLike, mode?: number): void
entries.description: existsSync reports whether the path exists and never throws; accessSync throws Node's error when the process lacks the access mode (F_OK, R_OK, W_OK, X_OK).

entries.name: fs.statSync / lstatSync / fstatSync
entries.signature: statSync(path: PathLike, options?: { throwIfNoEntry? }): Stats
entries.description: Node's Stats: the numeric fields (dev, mode, nlink, uid, gid, rdev, blksize, ino, size, blocks, atimeMs, mtimeMs, ctimeMs, birthtimeMs), the atime/mtime/ctime/birthtime Dates and the kind predicates. throwIfNoEntry: false returns undefined for a missing path. On Linux the stat is statx, so birthtime is real.
entries.snippet:
const st = fs.statSync('/tmp/out.txt')
console.log(st.size, st.isFile(), st.mtime)

entries.name: fs.statfsSync(path) → StatFs
entries.signature: statfsSync(path: PathLike): StatFs
entries.description: File-system statistics of the volume holding path: { type, bsize, frsize, blocks, bfree, bavail, files, ffree }.
differences: `{ bigint: true }` is ignored: the fields are numbers.

entries.name: fs.mkdirSync / mkdtempSync / rmdirSync / rmSync / unlinkSync
entries.signature: mkdirSync(path, options?: Mode | { recursive?, mode? }): string | undefined; rmSync(path, options?: { recursive?, force? }): void
entries.description: Directory creation (recursive returns the first directory made), temporary directories, and removal: rmSync removes a tree with recursive and ignores a missing path with force; a directory without recursive is Node's ERR_FS_EISDIR.
entries.snippet:
fs.mkdirSync('/tmp/a/b/c', { recursive: true })
fs.rmSync('/tmp/a', { recursive: true, force: true })

entries.name: fs.readdirSync(path[, options])
entries.signature: readdirSync(path, options?: { encoding?, withFileTypes?, recursive? }): string[] | Buffer[] | Dirent[]
entries.description: A directory's entries, sorted as libuv sorts them: names, Buffers with encoding: 'buffer', or Dirents (name, parentPath, the kind predicates) with withFileTypes; recursive walks the subtree breadth-first.
entries.snippet: for (const d of fs.readdirSync('.', { withFileTypes: true })) console.log(d.name, d.isDirectory())
differences: `dirent.path` (removed in Node v24) is a compile-time error rather than `undefined`.

entries.name: fs.renameSync / copyFileSync / linkSync / symlinkSync / readlinkSync / realpathSync
entries.statusRow: fs.renameSync / copyFileSync / linkSync / symlinkSync / readlinkSync / realpathSync
entries.signature: renameSync(oldPath, newPath): void; copyFileSync(src, dest, mode?): void; realpathSync(path): string
entries.description: Moving, copying (the copy takes the source's mode; COPYFILE_EXCL refuses an existing destination), hard and symbolic links, and path canonicalization: realpathSync is Node's lstat walk, realpathSync.native is realpath(3). Two-path errors name both paths.

entries.name: fs.openSync / closeSync / readSync / writeSync / readvSync / writevSync
entries.statusRow: fs.openSync / closeSync / readSync / writeSync / readvSync / writevSync
entries.signature: openSync(path, flags?, mode?): number; readSync(fd, buffer, offset?, length?, position?): number; writeSync(fd, data, …): number
entries.description: The descriptor-level API: open with any flag string or a numeric mask, read and write buffers (offset, length, position, or an options object) or strings (position, encoding), scatter/gather, close.

entries.name: fs.fsyncSync / fdatasyncSync / ftruncateSync / truncateSync
entries.signature: fsyncSync(fd): void; ftruncateSync(fd, len?): void; truncateSync(path, len?): void
entries.description: Flush a descriptor to disk and resize a file, by descriptor or path.

entries.name: fs.chmodSync / fchmodSync / chownSync / fchownSync / lchownSync
entries.signature: chmodSync(path, mode: number | string): void; chownSync(path, uid, gid): void
entries.description: Permission bits (a number or an octal string) and ownership, by path or descriptor. The chown family does nothing on Windows, as libuv's.

entries.name: fs.utimesSync / futimesSync / lutimesSync
entries.signature: utimesSync(path, atime: number | string | Date, mtime: number | string | Date): void
entries.description: Set access and modification times, as seconds, a numeric string or a Date, by path, descriptor or link.

entries.name: Callback forms
entries.statusRow: Callback forms (fs.readFile(path, cb) and the other operations)
entries.signature: fs.readFile(path[, options], cb); fs.stat(path, cb); fs.mkdir(path[, options], cb); …
entries.description: Every operation's callback form: each request runs on the thread pool and calls back on the event loop, as libuv's do. readFile and writeFile take an AbortSignal.
entries.snippet: fs.readFile('config.json', 'utf8', (err, text) => { if (err) throw err; console.log(text) })

entries.name: fs.promises / fs/promises
entries.signature: import { readFile, writeFile, stat, readdir, … } from 'fs/promises'
entries.description: Node's promise API: each function is its callback form's request settling a promise; readFile/writeFile/appendFile also take a FileHandle.

entries.name: fs.open / read / write / writev / readv / fsync / close
entries.statusRow: fs.open / close / read / write / writev / readv / fsync (callback form)
entries.signature: fs.open(path, flags?, mode?, cb); fs.read(fd, buffer, offset, length, position, cb); fs.write(fd, data, …, cb)
entries.description: The descriptor-level callback operations with Node's argument forms, validation errors and system errors.
differences: On Windows a positioned read or write seeks, then transfers: not atomic against another operation on the same descriptor.

entries.name: fsPromises.open → FileHandle
entries.signature: open(path, flags?, mode?): Promise<FileHandle>
entries.description: Opens a file and resolves to a FileHandle: fd, read, write, writev, sync, datasync, stat, truncate, chmod, utimes, readFile, writeFile, appendFile, createReadStream/createWriteStream, and close, which waits for the streams that hold the handle.

entries.name: fs.createReadStream / createWriteStream
entries.signature: fs.createReadStream(path, options?): fs.ReadStream; fs.createWriteStream(path, options?): fs.WriteStream
entries.description: Readable and Writable streams over a file, with Node's options (start/end, flags, mode, fd, fs, signal, autoClose, emitClose, flush, highWaterMark). Node's lib/internal/fs/streams.js.

entries.name: fs.watch
entries.signature: fs.watch(filename, options?, listener?): FSWatcher
entries.description: Native, event-driven change watching in the event loop: an FSWatcher (an EventEmitter) emitting 'change' with (eventType, filename), and 'close'. Backends: inotify, kqueue, ReadDirectoryChangesW.
entries.snippet: const w = fs.watch('config.json', (ev, name) => { console.log(ev, name); w.close() })
differences: On macOS a directory's event names the directory, not the changed entry.
`recursive` and `persistent: false` are validated and not applied.

entries.name: fs.constants
entries.signature: fs.constants: { O_*, S_*, F_OK, R_OK, W_OK, X_OK, COPYFILE_*, UV_* }
entries.description: Node's per-platform constants table, a real object.

entries.name: fs.cp / opendir / glob / watchFile / openAsBlob / lchmod
entries.statusRow: fs.cp / opendir → Dir / glob / watchFile / openAsBlob / lchmod
entries.signature: // not supported yet
entries.description: Not ported yet.

entries.name: File / FileReader / FileSystemFileHandle
entries.signature: // not supported
entries.description: The browser-flavored File API is not planned — these model browser sandbox/permission concepts this compiler has no equivalent for. A native CLI/microservice program has direct filesystem access via the fs functions above instead.
